description:
Confirmed by probe in bd:JMAP-1rwf.3 (commit pending). A peer that emits the naive camelCase 'icalComponent' (lowercase i) instead of the spec spelling 'iCalComponent' (capital I, capital C) deserializes silently:

  - typed CalendarEvent.ical_component = None
  - CalendarEvent.extra['icalComponent'] = the raw value
  - re-serialize preserves the lowercase spelling

Application code reading .ical_component will see None and conclude no iCalendar data was provided, even though the bytes are present in extras. Pinned in regression test calendar_event_naive_icalcomponent_lands_in_extras_not_typed_field (so any future change is visible).

The hazard is also documented in:
  - src/event.rs ical_component rustdoc
  - README.md Gotchas section

This bead is the mitigation-decision follow-up. Two options:

(a) Add #[serde(alias = "icalComponent")] to the ical_component field. On deserialize, both spellings populate the typed field. On serialize, the canonical 'iCalComponent' is emitted (a normalization side-effect — the non-conformant peer never learns). The regression test would need updating to assert the new typed-field destination. Public-API impact: a name that was previously bouncing into 'extra' now lands in the typed field; this CAN break a consumer who was reading extras directly (none in-tree).

(b) Do nothing further. The probe + regression test + Gotchas documentation are the deliverable; non-conformant peers stay broken; consumers who interop with such peers explicitly check extras.

Recommendation: option (a). Arguments:
  - The non-conformant spelling is already preserved by extras; option (a) just routes it into the typed field where it semantically belongs.
  - Serde aliases are exactly the mechanism for accepting wire-format variants while emitting one canonical form.
  - The 'silent normalization' downside is real but limited: the non-conformant peer never sees its bug on a round-trip, but the bug also doesn't cause silent data loss for downstream consumers. Net-better.
  - No in-tree consumer reads .extra['icalComponent'] directly, so the API break is theoretical.

Arguments against option (a):
  - The workspace AGENTS.md 'Caller contract' section is strict about typed-field/extras separation. Adding aliases changes which fields get diverted out of extras and could surprise a future contributor inserting into extras manually.
  - 'Silent acceptance' of a malformed wire form is a category of bug that has bit other implementations (e.g. HTTP header capitalization tolerance).

This decision is human-owned because it is a public-API + wire-format-compat call. Either option is defensible. If (a) is chosen, also: update the regression test, and decide whether to apply the same pattern to other brand-spelled fields in the workspace (none currently known).
title: calendars-types: decide mitigation for iCalComponent brand-mismatch hazard (confirmed)
